about: The curated deck factory works through this list from the top. See docs/curated-themes/factory.md.

themes.name: English History
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining moment of English history, Stonehenge to the present

themes.name: Indonesia
themes.scope: Yes if it happened in what is now Indonesia

themes.name: Kings of England
themes.scope: Yes if it is a monarch's accession, death or defining act

themes.name: Assassinations
themes.scope: Yes if a named person was killed for political reasons

themes.name: Automata
themes.scope: Yes if it is a machine built to act on its own

themes.name: Codes & Ciphers
themes.scope: Yes if it makes or breaks secret writing

themes.name: Clockwork
themes.scope: Yes if it is a device or convention for measuring time

themes.name: Cosmic Ideas
themes.scope: Yes if it is an idea about what the universe is

themes.name: Bridges & Tunnels
themes.scope: Yes if it is a built crossing of water, valley or rock

themes.name: Eureka Moments
themes.scope: Yes if it is the specific moment a discovery landed

themes.name: The Games Board
themes.scope: Yes if it is a game played at a table, or a machine that beat us at one

themes.name: Let There Be Light
themes.scope: Yes if it is a way of making artificial light

themes.name: Lost & Found
themes.scope: Yes if something buried was found, or a dead script read

themes.name: Mapmakers
themes.scope: Yes if it changed what people thought the world looked like

themes.name: Hard Currency
themes.scope: Yes if it is a form of money, or the institution issuing one

themes.name: Nations of Europe
themes.scope: Yes if it is the founding moment of a European country

themes.name: Numbers & Proofs
themes.scope: Yes if it is a mathematical idea entering human thought

themes.name: Plague Years
themes.scope: Yes if it is a named outbreak, or a decisive step in ending one

themes.name: The Deep
themes.scope: Yes if it is going deliberately under water, or finding what sank

themes.name: When the Earth Moved
themes.scope: Yes if it is an eruption, earthquake or tsunami

themes.name: What We Drink
themes.scope: Yes if it is a drink made on purpose, or a rule about drinking it

themes.name: Before Us
themes.scope: Yes if it happened before Homo sapiens existed

themes.name: Capitals Founded
themes.scope: Yes if it founded a city that is a national capital today

themes.name: Cities Ablaze
themes.scope: Yes if a city burned, or it is a step in fighting urban fire

themes.name: Ends of the Earth
themes.scope: Yes if people first reached a pole, a summit or an unvisited extreme

themes.name: Famine Years
themes.scope: Yes if it is a named famine, or a decisive step in ending one

themes.name: Mandate of Heaven
themes.scope: Yes if it is a Chinese dynasty's founding, peak act or fall

themes.name: On Stage
themes.scope: Yes if it is a stage form, a landmark premiere or a famous playhouse

themes.name: Peace at Last
themes.scope: Yes if it is a treaty or armistice that ended a named war

themes.name: Pharaohs
themes.scope: Yes if it is an act of an Egyptian ruler, Narmer to Cleopatra

themes.name: Pirates & Privateers
themes.scope: Yes if it is armed robbery at sea, or the war on it

themes.name: Places of Learning
themes.scope: Yes if it founded or destroyed a school, university or great library

themes.name: Sail & Steam
themes.scope: Yes if it is a new kind of ship, or one vessel that changed seafaring

themes.name: Stolen!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous theft, robbery or fraud carried out for gain

themes.name: Taking Flight
themes.scope: Yes if a person left the ground in a craft (atmosphere only)

themes.name: Tallest in the World
themes.scope: Yes if it became the tallest structure of its day, or let us build up

themes.name: Tamed
themes.scope: Yes if it is an animal brought into human service

themes.name: The First Woman
themes.scope: Yes if it is the first time a woman did or held something

themes.name: The Roman Story
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining moment of the Roman state, to 1453

themes.name: Under Siege
themes.scope: Yes if it is the siege of a named city or fortress

themes.name: Under the Knife
themes.scope: Yes if it is a surgical procedure or tool, or a way to survive one

themes.name: Walls & Fortresses
themes.scope: Yes if it built or brought down a fortification meant to keep people out

themes.name: Waterworks
themes.scope: Yes if it moves or holds back water by design

themes.name: Dinosaurs
themes.scope: Yes if it is a dinosaur, dated to when it lived, or a turning point in the dinosaurs' own story
themes.boundary: Dinosaurs owns the animals themselves and the bookends of their reign; their discovery goes to Bone Hunters, and the life around them (mammals, pterosaurs, sea reptiles, flowering plants) stays in Before Us.
example_beats: Eoraptor, one of the first dinosaurs (231 million years ago)
Coelophysis hunts in packs (215 million years ago)
Plateosaurus, an early long-neck (214 million years ago)
Archaeopteryx, the first bird (150 million years ago)
The asteroid ends their reign (66 million years ago)
themes.notes: One beat per dinosaur, dated to the start of its fossil range (the range in `note`), plus the first dinosaurs and the asteroid. Spread the beats across the Triassic, Jurassic and Cretaceous by their length. Never name a period or 'million years' on a card.

themes.name: The Caesars
themes.scope: Yes if it is a Roman or Byzantine emperor coming to the throne
themes.boundary: The Caesars owns each emperor's accession; every other moment of the Roman state stays in The Roman Story.
example_beats: Vespasian ends the Year of Four Emperors (69)
themes.notes: One beat per emperor, dated to his accession, from Augustus to the fall of Constantinople. Prefer the famous, and give Byzantium its share.

themes.name: Age of Mammals
themes.scope: Yes if it is a mammal of the last 66 million years, dated to when it lived
themes.boundary: Age of Mammals owns mammals from the asteroid to the end of the Ice Age; dinosaurs go to Dinosaurs, human species to Our Ancestors, extinctions in the human era to Gone Forever.
example_beats: Purgatorius, an early primate relative (66 million years ago)
Eohippus, the dawn horse (55 million years ago)
Ambulocetus, the walking whale (49 million years ago)
Paraceratherium, the largest land mammal (34 million years ago)
Megatherium, the giant ground sloth (5 million years ago)
Smilodon, the sabre-tooth (2.5 million years ago)
themes.notes: One beat per animal, dated to the start of its fossil range, spread across all 66 million years by length, not crowded into the Ice Age. Never name an epoch or 'million years' on a card.

themes.name: Rise of Empires
themes.scope: Yes if it is the founding of a great empire
themes.boundary: Rise of Empires owns each empire's founding; its rulers and later story stay with its own theme, such as The Roman Story, Mandate of Heaven, Sublime Porte or Peacock Throne.
example_beats: Sargon founds the Akkadian Empire (2334 BC)
Cyrus founds the Persian Empire (550 BC)
Chandragupta founds the Maurya Empire (322 BC)
Genghis Khan founds the Mongol Empire (1206)
themes.notes: Date each empire to its founding or its founder's first conquest, one beat per empire, spread across every continent.

themes.name: The Great Composers
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous work by a great composer of classical music
themes.boundary: The Great Composers owns classical composers' signature works; instruments go to Strike a Chord, anthems and songs for a cause to Sing Out!
themes.notes: One beat per composer, dated to the premiere or publication of their best-known work, spread from medieval chant to the present.

themes.name: Our Ancestors
themes.scope: Yes if it is a human species or ancestor, or a milestone of human evolution
themes.boundary: Our Ancestors owns hominins dated to when they lived; their fossil finds go to Bone Hunters, and what Homo sapiens made to Stone Age Firsts.
example_beats: Humans leave Africa (1.8 million years ago)
The Hobbit of Flores (100,000 years ago)
themes.notes: One beat per species, dated to the start of its fossil range, plus milestones such as walking upright, tools, fire and leaving Africa to reach 30. Never name an epoch or 'million years' on a card.

themes.name: Mr President
themes.scope: Yes if it is a US president taking office
themes.boundary: Mr President owns US presidents' inaugurations; the elections themselves go to The Ballot Box.
themes.notes: One beat per president, dated to his first inauguration, from Washington to 2009. Later presidents are live politics, so leave them out.

themes.name: Big Thinkers
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining work or teaching of a great philosopher
themes.boundary: Big Thinkers owns philosophy; scientific discoveries go to Eureka Moments, and the founding of religions to Faith Founded.
example_beats: Descartes: I think, therefore I am (1637)
themes.notes: One beat per thinker, dated to their defining work or teaching, spread across East and West and from the ancients to the present.

themes.name: Ages of the Earth
themes.scope: Yes if it is the start of an eon, era, period or epoch of Earth's history
themes.boundary: Ages of the Earth owns the geological time scale itself; the life and events within it stay in Before Us, Dinosaurs and Age of Mammals.
example_beats: The Hadean begins (4.6 billion years ago)
The Cryogenian, Snowball Earth (720 million years ago)
themes.notes: One beat per unit, dated to its start on the official time scale, Hadean to Holocene. The card names the unit; its description shows the world then, never a number of years. Skip it if 30 can't be found.

themes.name: Sweet Tooth
themes.scope: Yes if it is a sweet treat
themes.boundary: Sweet Tooth: candy, chocolate, biscuits and desserts; savoury dishes go to Born in a Kitchen, canning and freezing to Food Tech, cocoa and other drinks to What We Drink.
example_beats: Fry's makes the first chocolate bar (1847)
Ice cream cone at the St Louis fair (1904)

themes.name: Sublime Porte
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining moment of the Ottoman Empire
themes.boundary: Sublime Porte: the Ottoman story; the great sieges (Vienna, Malta) go to Under Siege, caliphs before 1517 to The Caliphs, Lepanto to Broadsides.

themes.name: Silicon Dreams
themes.scope: Yes if it is a computer, chip or other computing hardware
themes.boundary: Silicon Dreams: the machines; mechanical calculators go to Automata, wartime codebreaking machines to Codes & Ciphers, software to Hello, World, pocket devices to In Your Pocket.

themes.name: The Liberators
themes.scope: Yes if it is part of Latin America's struggle for independence
themes.boundary: The Liberators: Latin American independence wars; the Spanish conquest goes to Conquistadors, the end of slavery to Chains Broken, Tupac Amaru's rising to Rise Up!
example_beats: Spain loses Cuba and Puerto Rico (1898)

themes.name: Gone Forever
themes.scope: Yes if it is a species going extinct
themes.boundary: Gone Forever owns extinctions in the human era, last named survivors such as Martha included; mass extinctions and prehistoric species go to Before Us, rescue and protection to Back from the Brink.

themes.name: Whodunit
themes.scope: Yes if it is a detective or crime novel, or a famous sleuth's debut
themes.boundary: Whodunit: invented crimes and sleuths; real police and prisons go to Crime & Punishment, horror to Fright Night, spies to Spy Games.
example_beats: Poe's Murders in the Rue Morgue (1841)
Poirot debuts in The Mysterious Affair at Styles (1920)
The Big Sleep introduces Philip Marlowe (1939)

themes.name: Day in Court
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous trial or court ruling
themes.boundary: Day in Court: the courtroom; civil-rights rulings share with Civil Rights Road, trials of books, Galileo's included, go to Banned!, police and prisons to Crime & Punishment, written law to Law of the Land.

themes.name: Black Gold
themes.scope: Yes if it is a milestone in oil or gas
themes.boundary: Black Gold: oil and gas; gold and diamond rushes go to Strike It Rich, other industrial blasts to When It Went Wrong, lamp oil to Let There Be Light.

themes.name: Rise Up!
themes.scope: Yes if it is an uprising of ordinary people against their rulers
themes.boundary: Rise Up!: popular uprisings, Pugachev and the Paris Commune included; plots and putsches go to Coup!, peaceful marches to Take to the Streets, wars of independence to The Liberators, the 1857 rebellion to The Raj.

themes.name: The Romanovs
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining moment of Romanov Russia
themes.boundary: The Romanovs: Russia from 1613 to 1917, Catherine the Great included; communism goes to Red Flags, Pugachev's revolt to Rise Up!.

themes.name: Message Sent
themes.scope: Yes if it is a way of sending a message or parcel across distance
themes.boundary: Message Sent: carried or wired messages and mail; broadcasting goes to Tune In, the internet to Going Online, pocket gadgets to In Your Pocket.
example_beats: Augustus creates the Cursus Publicus (27 BC)
Morse sends the first telegraph message (1844)

themes.name: Before Columbus
themes.scope: Yes if it is from the pre-Columbian Americas
themes.boundary: Before Columbus: Maya, Aztec, Inca and earlier worlds; the Spanish conquest goes to Conquistadors, peoples of the US and Canada to Native Nations, Tenochtitlan's founding to Capitals Founded.
example_beats: Olmec rise at San Lorenzo (1200 BC)
Pakal takes the throne at Palenque (615)

themes.name: Votes for Women
themes.scope: Yes if it is women winning the vote, or the fight for it
themes.boundary: Votes for Women owns women's suffrage; other voting milestones go to The Ballot Box, other women's firsts to The First Woman.

themes.name: Sell, Sell, Sell
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous advertisement, slogan or brand mascot
themes.boundary: Sell, Sell, Sell: the pitch itself; shops go to Retail Therapy, the founding of companies to Still Trading, broadcast milestones to Tune In.
example_beats: Caxton prints one of the first advertisements (1477)
Old Spice 'The Man Your Man Could Smell Like' (2010)

themes.name: Seeing Inside
themes.scope: Yes if it is a way of looking inside or testing the body
themes.boundary: Seeing Inside owns diagnosis and scanning; the discovery of X-rays goes to Eureka Moments, operations to Under the Knife, drugs to Wonder Drugs, genetics to Code of Life.
example_beats: First MRI scan of a human (1977)

themes.name: Face to Face
themes.scope: Yes if it is a summit of rulers or an embassy to a foreign court
themes.boundary: Face to Face: meetings and missions; war-ending treaties, Tilsit included, go to Peace at Last, Cold War crises to Iron Curtain, merchants and pilgrims on the caravan roads to Silk Road.
example_beats: Ibn Fadlan's embassy to the Volga (921)
Field of the Cloth of Gold (1520)
Macartney's embassy to the Qianlong Emperor (1793)

themes.name: Live Wire
themes.scope: Yes if it is a way of making, storing or moving electric power
themes.boundary: Live Wire: electric power and its grids, batteries included; lamps go to Let There Be Light, dams to Waterworks, nuclear stations to The Atomic Age, Faraday's induction to Eureka Moments.

themes.name: Faiths of Asia
themes.scope: Yes if it is a milestone of Buddhism, Hinduism or another Asian faith
themes.boundary: Faiths of Asia: Asia's religions, their founding and Sikhism included; temples as buildings go to Houses of Worship, Islam to The Caliphs, the Diamond Sutra to Letters & Type.
example_beats: Zhang Daoling founds the Celestial Masters (142)

themes.name: Dress Code
themes.scope: Yes if it is a garment, fabric or fashion house
themes.boundary: Dress Code: clothes and the cloth they are cut from, spinning and weaving machines and new fibres included; engines and factory methods go to Made by Machine, the ads behind brands to Sell, Sell, Sell, other new materials to Material World.
example_beats: Charles Worth opens a Paris couture house (1858)

themes.name: Faith Founded
themes.scope: Yes if it is the founding of a religion, sect or religious order
themes.boundary: Faith Founded owns the beginnings of faiths, sects and orders; Asia's religions and Sikhism go to Faiths of Asia, the papacy to Habemus Papam, the caliphate to The Caliphs.
example_beats: Joseph Smith founds the Church of Christ (1830)

themes.name: In Your Pocket
themes.scope: Yes if it is a phone or other gadget you carry around
themes.boundary: In Your Pocket: carry-anywhere devices; watches go to Clockwork, handheld game consoles to Insert Coin, recorded-music formats to Press Play, home appliances to Household Gadgets.
example_beats: Motorola makes the first mobile phone call (1973)
Nokia 1011 and the SMS era begin (1992)

themes.name: Flying Colours
themes.scope: Yes if it is a country's flag first being raised
themes.boundary: Flying Colours: a national flag first raised or adopted; independence itself goes to Flags Come Down, countries' founding moments to Nations of Europe, colonial footholds to Flag Planted.
example_beats: The Dannebrog falls from the sky at Lyndanisse (1219)
The Flag Act adopts the Stars and Stripes (1777)
Italy's tricolore first flown at Reggio Emilia (1797)
The Union Flag gains the cross of St Patrick (1801)
Brazil raises its green and gold flag (1889)
The Australian flag is first flown (1901)
themes.notes: Famous flags only, dated to when each was first hoisted or officially adopted.

themes.name: Peacock Throne
themes.scope: Yes if it is an act of a Delhi sultan or Mughal emperor
themes.boundary: Peacock Throne: Muslim rulers of Delhi and the Mughal court, the Taj Mahal and Timur's sack of Delhi included; the Company's rise goes to The Raj, Persian shahs to Kings of Kings, Ottoman sultans to Sublime Porte, Razia Sultana to Crowned Queens.
example_beats: Qutb ud-Din Aibak founds the Delhi Sultanate (1206)
Tughluq moves the capital to Daulatabad (1327)
Shah Jahan begins the Taj Mahal (1632)

themes.name: Strike It Rich
themes.scope: Yes if it is a gold, silver or diamond strike or rush
themes.boundary: Strike It Rich: rushes and finds of precious metals and gems; oil goes to Black Gold, the conquest that found Potosi to Conquistadors.

themes.name: War Machines
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous weapon or fighting machine
themes.boundary: War Machines: weapons from Greek fire to drones; nuclear bombs go to The Atomic Age, rockets as launchers to Lift-Off!, warship designs to Sail & Steam.

themes.name: Taxing Times
themes.scope: Yes if it is a tax, tariff or census
themes.boundary: Taxing Times: what states took and counted; the revolts taxes sparked go to Rise Up!, the Boston Tea Party to What We Drink, money itself to Hard Currency.

themes.name: Scramble for Africa
themes.scope: Yes if it is a foreign expedition, claim or conquest in Africa
themes.boundary: Scramble for Africa: outsiders' expeditions and claims in Africa and the resistance to them; forts and colonies such as Elmina and Cape Town go to Flag Planted, African states' own story to African Kingdoms, independence to Flags Come Down.

themes.name: Platinum
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous album
themes.boundary: Platinum: the albums themselves; single anthems, protest songs and charity singles go to Sing Out!, the birth of styles to Born to Groove, concerts to Crowd Roars, formats such as the LP to Press Play.
example_beats: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band (1967)
The Dark Side of the Moon (1973)

themes.name: Mind the Gap
themes.scope: Yes if it is the opening of a city metro, tram or bus system
themes.boundary: Mind the Gap owns urban transit; intercity railways go to All Aboard!, tunnels as engineering feats to Bridges & Tunnels.

themes.name: The Caliphs
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining act of a caliph or caliphate
themes.boundary: The Caliphs owns the caliphate; Ottoman sultans go to Sublime Porte, the Crusades to The Crusades, schools and libraries to Places of Learning.

themes.name: Inside the Mind
themes.scope: Yes if it is a landmark of psychology, psychiatry or brain science
themes.boundary: Inside the Mind owns the mind and brain, psychiatric drugs included; other medicines go to Wonder Drugs, scanners to Seeing Inside.

themes.name: Letters & Type
themes.scope: Yes if it is a milestone in printing, typing or typefaces
themes.boundary: Letters & Type: the look and mechanics of text, the Diamond Sutra and Jikji included; secret writing goes to Codes & Ciphers, Hangul to Korean Wave, reference books to Look It Up.
example_beats: Jikji printed with metal type in Korea (1377)

themes.name: Code of Life
themes.scope: Yes if it is a step in discovering or editing DNA and genes
themes.boundary: Code of Life owns genetics; evolution and natural history go to Field Notes, scanning to Seeing Inside, domesticated animals to Tamed.

themes.name: Between the Rivers
themes.scope: Yes if it is an event of Sumer, Babylon or Assyria
themes.boundary: Between the Rivers: Sumer, Babylon and Assyria; Persia from Cyrus on goes to Kings of Kings, sieges to Under Siege, Egypt to Pharaohs, Ashurbanipal's library to Places of Learning.
example_beats: Uruk becomes the first city (c. 3500 BC)
Sargon of Akkad founds his empire (2334 BC)
Sennacherib builds his Nineveh palace (700 BC)

themes.name: Iron Curtain
themes.scope: Yes if it is a Cold War crisis or proxy war
themes.boundary: Iron Curtain: the blocs' confrontation, the Berlin Wall and the Cuban Missile Crisis included; bombs and arms treaties go to The Atomic Age, alliances to Safety in Numbers, communism's own revolutions to Red Flags, spies to Spy Games.

themes.name: Houses of Worship
themes.scope: Yes if it is the building of a famous temple, church, mosque or shrine
themes.boundary: Houses of Worship: sacred buildings; spires that set height records go to Tallest in the World, Angkor Wat to Temple Kingdoms, the Golden Temple to Faiths of Asia, the Dome of the Rock to The Caliphs, Hagia Sophia to The Roman Story.

themes.name: Take to the Streets
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous protest march or demonstration
themes.boundary: Take to the Streets: protests and marches; strikes go to Down Tools, racial-equality protests to Civil Rights Road, Gandhi's Salt March to The Raj, armed uprisings to Rise Up!

themes.name: Habemus Papam
themes.scope: Yes if it is a moment in the history of the papacy
themes.boundary: Habemus Papam owns popes and councils; religious beginnings go to Faith Founded, the Crusades to The Crusades.
example_beats: Council of Constance ends the Western Schism (1417)

themes.name: Crime & Punishment
themes.scope: Yes if it is a milestone in policing or punishing crime
themes.boundary: Crime & Punishment: police, prisons and detection; trials go to Day in Court, invented detectives to Whodunit, robberies to Stolen!
example_beats: Alcatraz opens as a federal prison (1934)

themes.name: Crowd Roars
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous concert, tour or music festival
themes.boundary: Crowd Roars: a dated live performance or music festival; carnivals and parades go to Let's Celebrate, opera and theatre premieres to On Stage.

themes.name: Material World
themes.scope: Yes if it is a material people learned to make
themes.boundary: Material World: new stuff to make things from, copper and bronze to plastics; fibres such as nylon go to Dress Code, tall-building steel to Tallest in the World, writing surfaces to Letters & Type.

themes.name: Civil Rights Road
themes.scope: Yes if it is a moment in a fight for racial equality
themes.boundary: Civil Rights Road: struggles against segregation and racial discrimination anywhere, the US and South Africa included; ending slavery goes to Chains Broken, other marches to Take to the Streets, other trials to Day in Court.

themes.name: Taking Measure
themes.scope: Yes if it is a unit, scale or standard of measurement
themes.boundary: Taking Measure owns units and scales, the Richter scale included; clocks, calendars and Greenwich time go to Clockwork, weather instruments to Weather Eye, maps to Mapmakers.

themes.name: Funny Pages
themes.scope: Yes if it is a comic strip, comic book or comics hero
themes.boundary: Funny Pages: comics; manga share a few with Cool Japan, animated cartoons go to Drawn to Life.

themes.name: Chains Broken
themes.scope: Yes if it is a step toward ending slavery or serfdom
themes.boundary: Chains Broken owns abolition and emancipation, the Emancipation Proclamation and 13th Amendment included; revolts go to Rise Up!, the later fight against segregation to Civil Rights Road, Haiti's revolution to The Liberators.

themes.name: Pedal & Petrol
themes.scope: Yes if it is a milestone of the car, motorcycle or bicycle
themes.boundary: Pedal & Petrol: road vehicles with wheels; company foundings go to Still Trading, roads to The Open Road, factory methods to Made by Machine.
example_beats: First mountain bikes in Marin County (1977)

themes.name: Horse Lords
themes.scope: Yes if it is a deed of the steppe nomads, from Scythians to Mongols
themes.boundary: Horse Lords: Scythians, Huns, Turks, Seljuks and the Mongol empire; China's own dynasties, the Yuan included, go to Mandate of Heaven, caravan trade to Silk Road, Timur in Delhi to Peacock Throne, the Mongol fleets off Japan to Shogun!, Hungary's and Bulgaria's founding to Nations of Europe.

themes.name: When It Went Wrong
themes.scope: Yes if it is an industrial or engineering disaster
themes.boundary: When It Went Wrong: engineering failures; bridge collapses go to Bridges & Tunnels, dam bursts other than Vajont to Waterworks, fires to Cities Ablaze, nuclear accidents to The Atomic Age, oil spills to Black Gold.

themes.name: Conquistadors
themes.scope: Yes if it is part of the Spanish conquest or colonisation of the Americas
themes.boundary: Conquistadors: Spain in the Americas; Columbus's crossing goes to Landfall!, the civilisations before it to Before Columbus, cities still capitals today to Capitals Founded, silver rushes to Strike It Rich.
example_beats: Coronado hunts the Seven Cities of Gold (1540)
Last Inca ruler Tupac Amaru executed (1572)

themes.name: Press Play
themes.scope: Yes if it is a way of recording, selling or hearing music
themes.boundary: Press Play: the music business and its formats; instruments go to Strike a Chord, radio and TV to Tune In, pocket players such as the Walkman and iPod to In Your Pocket, which owns them.

themes.name: Pens Over Swords
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous book or pamphlet of political ideas
themes.boundary: Pens Over Swords: political thought in print; the Communist Manifesto goes to Red Flags, constitutions to Law of the Land, books that were banned to Banned!
example_beats: Burke's Reflections on the Revolution in France (1790)
Wollstonecraft's Vindication of the Rights of Woman (1792)

themes.name: Spy Games
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous spy, spy ring or espionage operation
themes.boundary: Spy Games: espionage; making and breaking codes goes to Codes & Ciphers, Cold War crises to Iron Curtain, political murders to Assassinations.
example_beats: U-2 pilot Gary Powers shot down (1960)

themes.name: Made by Machine
themes.scope: Yes if it is an engine, machine tool or factory method
themes.boundary: Made by Machine: engines, tools and factories; textile machines go to Dress Code, robots to Automata, steel for skyscrapers to Tallest in the World.

themes.name: Wonder Drugs
themes.scope: Yes if it is a medicine or drug being discovered or first used
themes.boundary: Wonder Drugs owns medicines; vaccines and epidemics go to Plague Years, psychiatric landmarks to Inside the Mind, operations to Under the Knife.
example_beats: Insulin first used on a patient (1922)

themes.name: Sing Out!
themes.scope: Yes if it is an anthem or a song for a cause
themes.boundary: Sing Out!: songs that carry a cause, charity singles included; albums go to Platinum, the birth of styles to Born to Groove, benefit concerts to Crowd Roars.
example_beats: God Save the King first performed (1745)

themes.name: Other Worlds
themes.scope: Yes if it is a spacecraft reaching another world
themes.boundary: Other Worlds: probes and landings beyond Earth orbit, the Moon landings included; Earth-orbit flights and rockets go to Lift-Off!, planets spotted from the ground to Stargazers.

themes.name: Beyond the Stars
themes.scope: Yes if it is a science fiction or fantasy book
themes.boundary: Beyond the Stars: speculative books; horror, Frankenstein included, goes to Fright Night, children's classics to Bedtime Stories, real space exploration to Other Worlds.
example_beats: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea (1870)
The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy (1979)

themes.name: Newfound Beasts
themes.scope: Yes if it is an animal first described to science or found alive
themes.boundary: Newfound Beasts owns an animal species coming to light; single famous animals go to Famous Animals, fossils to Bone Hunters, deep-sea exploration to The Deep.

themes.name: Unveiled!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous statue, memorial or monument
themes.boundary: Unveiled!: monuments that honour; pyramids go to Pharaohs, monuments that set height records to Tallest in the World, Mughal tombs to Peacock Throne.
example_beats: The Little Mermaid unveiled in Copenhagen (1913)

themes.name: Food Tech
themes.scope: Yes if it is a way of preserving or mass-producing food
themes.boundary: Food Tech: food from the factory; dishes from the kitchen go to Born in a Kitchen, sweets to Sweet Tooth, pasteurised drinks to What We Drink, fridges and microwaves to Household Gadgets.

themes.name: Against the Odds
themes.scope: Yes if it is a small force's famous victory or last stand
themes.boundary: Against the Odds: the few against the many in open battle; sieges, the Alamo included, go to Under Siege, Agincourt stays with Kings of England, Adwa with African Kingdoms.

themes.name: Famous Animals
themes.scope: Yes if it is a moment in the life of a famous individual animal
themes.boundary: Famous Animals owns named individual animals, space dogs, sled dogs and clones included; species-level stories go to Newfound Beasts, the last of a species to Gone Forever, kinds of animal put to work to Tamed.
example_beats: Ham the chimp flies into space (1961)
Koko the gorilla starts learning sign language (1972)

themes.name: The Crusades
themes.scope: Yes if it is a moment in the Crusades
themes.boundary: The Crusades owns the holy wars; its great sieges (Jerusalem, Antioch, Acre) share with Under Siege, the caliphate's story goes to The Caliphs, popes to Habemus Papam.
example_beats: Bernard preaches the Second Crusade at Vezelay (1146)
Frederick II regains Jerusalem by treaty (1229)

themes.name: Weather Eye
themes.scope: Yes if it is a landmark in understanding or forecasting weather and climate
themes.boundary: Weather Eye owns weather and climate science; extreme events go to Wild Weather, units and scales to Taking Measure, protecting wildlife to Back from the Brink.
example_beats: FitzRoy issues the first public forecast (1861)

themes.name: Isms
themes.scope: Yes if it is the launch of an art movement
themes.boundary: Isms: the birth of a movement; single famous paintings go to Gallery Greats, modern buildings to Modern Marvels.
example_beats: Fauvism debuts at the Salon d'Automne (1905)
Armory Show brings modern art to America (1913)

themes.name: The Atomic Age
themes.scope: Yes if it is a nuclear bomb, reactor, treaty or accident
themes.boundary: The Atomic Age: all things nuclear, arms treaties, civil power and its accidents included; fission's discovery stays with Eureka Moments, particles go to Building Blocks, the Cuban Missile Crisis to Iron Curtain.

themes.name: Cut a Rug
themes.scope: Yes if it is a dance or dance craze
themes.boundary: Cut a Rug: the dances themselves, folk, court and craze; music styles go to Born to Groove, ballet and stage premieres to On Stage, carnivals and parades to Let's Celebrate.
example_beats: Louis XIV founds the Royal Academy of Dance (1661)
The waltz sweeps the Congress of Vienna (1815)
Can-can at the new Moulin Rouge (1889)

themes.name: Crowned Queens
themes.scope: Yes if it is a woman ruling a country in her own right
themes.boundary: Crowned Queens owns women who ruled, Razia Sultana and Nzinga included; English and British queens go to Kings of England, Egypt's to Pharaohs, Catherine the Great to The Romanovs, other women's firsts to The First Woman.
example_beats: Irene becomes sole ruler of Byzantium (797)
Razia Sultana takes the Delhi throne (1236)
Maria Theresa inherits the Habsburg lands (1740)
Wilhelmina becomes Queen of the Netherlands (1890)

themes.name: Gallery Greats
themes.scope: Yes if it is a single famous painting
themes.boundary: Gallery Greats: one famous picture; statues and memorials go to Unveiled!, the movements behind them to Isms, their thefts to Stolen!

themes.name: Red Flags
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining act of communism or a communist state
themes.boundary: Red Flags: communism's own story inside its states; standoffs with the West, the Berlin Wall and Soviet tanks in Budapest and Prague go to Iron Curtain, the Paris Commune to Rise Up!, the Romanov fall to The Romanovs, other political books to Pens Over Swords.

themes.name: Front Pages
themes.scope: Yes if it is the launch of a newspaper or magazine
themes.boundary: Front Pages: newspapers and magazines; reference works go to Look It Up, broadcast news to Tune In.
example_beats: Relation, the first weekly paper, printed in Strasbourg (1605)

themes.name: Hello, World
themes.scope: Yes if it is a landmark of software or AI
themes.boundary: Hello, World: programs, languages and artificial intelligence; the machines go to Silicon Dreams, the web to Going Online, machines that beat us at chess or Go to The Games Board, Lovelace and Hopper to The First Woman.

themes.name: Cool Japan
themes.scope: Yes if it is Japanese pop culture
themes.boundary: Cool Japan: prints, films, manga, anime, characters and music, Godzilla and Ghibli included; video games go to Insert Coin, portable gadgets to In Your Pocket, the samurai age to Shogun!

themes.name: Field Notes
themes.scope: Yes if it is a naturalist's voyage, book or big idea about life
themes.boundary: Field Notes owns natural history, evolution's story included; Cook's Endeavour voyage goes to Landfall!, fossils to Bone Hunters, new species to Newfound Beasts, genes to Code of Life, TV shows to Prime Time.
example_beats: Merian's Metamorphosis of the Insects of Surinam (1705)
Gilbert White's Natural History of Selborne (1789)

themes.name: Going Online
themes.scope: Yes if it is a milestone of the internet or the web
themes.boundary: Going Online: networks, protocols, browsers, search and early online services; phones go to In Your Pocket, the machines to Silicon Dreams.

themes.name: Doors Open
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous museum or gallery opening
themes.boundary: Doors Open: museums and galleries; schools and libraries go to Places of Learning, other landmark buildings to Modern Marvels.

themes.name: Abdicated!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a monarch abdicating or being forced off the throne
themes.boundary: Abdicated!: thrones given up or lost, including the last emperors of fallen empires; the exiles that followed go to Banished!, plots to Coup!, the Romanov end shares with The Romanovs, English kings with Kings of England.

themes.name: Bedtime Stories
themes.scope: Yes if it is a children's book or fairy-tale collection
themes.boundary: Bedtime Stories: books for children, children's fantasy included; fantasy aimed at adults goes to Beyond the Stars, toys of the characters to Toy Box.
example_beats: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone (1997)

themes.name: Flag Planted
themes.scope: Yes if it is the founding of a colony or trading post
themes.boundary: Flag Planted: footholds abroad, from Elmina to Cape Town and Botany Bay; the voyages that found the coasts go to Landfall!, cities now national capitals to Capitals Founded, Spain's American towns to Conquistadors, later inland claims in Africa to Scramble for Africa.
example_beats: First Fleet lands at Sydney Cove (1788)

themes.name: The Open Road
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous road, highway or rule of the road
themes.boundary: The Open Road owns roads and traffic rules; vehicles go to Pedal & Petrol, bridges and tunnels to Bridges & Tunnels, Roman roads may also fit The Roman Story.

themes.name: Still Trading
themes.scope: Yes if it is the founding of a famous company that still exists
themes.boundary: Still Trading: the birth of a business, shop chains included; a firm's products go to the theme for what it makes (Pedal & Petrol, Insert Coin), restaurant chains to Order Up!, web platforms to Going Online, Coca-Cola to What We Drink, central banks to Hard Currency.
example_beats: Nokia founded as a paper mill (1865)

themes.name: Say Cheese
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous photograph or camera breakthrough
themes.boundary: Say Cheese: still photographs and cameras; moving pictures go to Roll Camera, phone cameras to In Your Pocket, Earthrise to Other Worlds, Tiananmen to Take to the Streets.
example_beats: V-J Day kiss in Times Square (1945)
Afghan Girl on the cover of National Geographic (1984)

themes.name: Lines on a Map
themes.scope: Yes if it is a border drawn or a territory bought, sold or swapped
themes.boundary: Lines on a Map: borders and land deals; treaties that ended wars go to Peace at Last, which owns the contested ones, alliances to Safety in Numbers, how maps were made to Mapmakers.

themes.name: Banished!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous exile or banishment
themes.boundary: Banished! owns exile; rulers fleeing or losing their thrones go to Abdicated!, communist leaders' careers to Red Flags.

themes.name: Broadsides
themes.scope: Yes if it is a naval battle
themes.boundary: Broadsides: fleet against fleet, Actium, the Armada and Trafalgar included; piracy goes to Pirates & Privateers, ship designs to Sail & Steam.

themes.name: Drawn to Life
themes.scope: Yes if it is a milestone in animation
themes.boundary: Drawn to Life: animated films, characters and techniques; animated TV series go to Prime Time, anime to Cool Japan, live-action effects to Roll Camera.

themes.name: Landfall!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a voyage of discovery across the sea
themes.boundary: Landfall!: voyages that found or crossed new waters, the Pacific included; the colonies that followed go to Flag Planted, polar pushes and summits to Ends of the Earth, ship designs to Sail & Steam.

themes.name: Meiji Leap
themes.scope: Yes if it is a milestone of Japan opening up and modernising
themes.boundary: Meiji Leap: Perry's arrival to the Meiji Emperor's death; the samurai age goes to Shogun!, constitutions share with Law of the Land, sea battles, Tsushima included, go to Broadsides.

themes.name: Modern Marvels
themes.scope: Yes if it is a celebrated modern building
themes.boundary: Modern Marvels: landmark modern design; record-height towers go to Tallest in the World, museums to Doors Open, world's fair pavilions to Step Right Up.

themes.name: Bad Science
themes.scope: Yes if it is a scientific hoax, fraud or blunder
themes.boundary: Bad Science: science gone wrong, harmful products sold as safe included; frauds for money go to Stolen!, medicines that worked to Wonder Drugs.

themes.name: Banned!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a book that was banned, burned or put on trial
themes.boundary: Banned!: books under attack; other famous trials go to Day in Court, destroyed libraries to Places of Learning, political classics that were never banned to Pens Over Swords.
example_beats: Ulysses banned in the United States (1921)
Grapes of Wrath burned in California (1939)

themes.name: Lift-Off!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a rocket or a flight in Earth orbit
themes.boundary: Lift-Off!: rockets and Earth-orbit flights; trips to the Moon and planets go to Other Worlds, space telescopes to Stargazers, rocket weapons to War Machines, atmosphere-only flight to Taking Flight.

themes.name: Born to Groove
themes.scope: Yes if it is a style of music
themes.boundary: Born to Groove: the birth of a music style; dances go to Cut a Rug, albums to Platinum, anthems and protest songs to Sing Out!.
example_beats: Chega de Saudade starts bossa nova (1958)
DJ Kool Herc's party sparks hip-hop (1973)
Strings of Life and Detroit techno (1987)

themes.name: Plow & Harvest
themes.scope: Yes if it is a tool or technique that changed farming
themes.boundary: Plow & Harvest owns farm machines and methods; crops on the move go to Plant Hunters, irrigation to Waterworks, starvation to Famine Years.

themes.name: Nobel Winners
themes.scope: Yes if it is the work that won a Nobel Prize
themes.boundary: Nobel Winners: the book, discovery or campaign a prize was given for, dated to when it was done; discoveries that are famous as the moment itself go to Eureka Moments and Building Blocks, the rights struggles to Civil Rights Road.
example_beats: The Old Man and the Sea (1952)
themes.notes: Date each card to the seminal work, not to the year of the prize.

themes.name: Korean Wave
themes.scope: Yes if it is a milestone of Korean culture, from Hangul to K-pop
themes.boundary: Korean Wave: Korea's cultural gifts, Hangul and Gangnam Style included; the Korean War goes to Iron Curtain, turtle ships to Broadsides, Seoul's founding to Capitals Founded.
example_beats: Nam June Paik's first video art show (1963)

themes.name: Master Plans
themes.scope: Yes if it is a planned city, new town or city plan
themes.boundary: Master Plans: cities and districts laid out by design; planned national capitals such as Brasilia and Canberra go to Capitals Founded, which owns them, and grand showpiece buildings to Palaces & Power.
example_beats: Shenzhen becomes a special economic zone (1980)

themes.name: Roll Camera
themes.scope: Yes if it is a landmark film or a breakthrough in filmmaking
themes.boundary: Roll Camera: live-action film and its machinery; animation goes to Drawn to Life, horror films to Fright Night, television to Tune In and Prime Time, still photography to Say Cheese.
example_beats: Lumiere brothers' first public film show (1895)
Gone with the Wind and The Wizard of Oz in Technicolor (1939)

themes.name: Kings of France
themes.scope: Yes if it is a French king's accession, death or defining act
themes.boundary: Kings of France owns the French monarchy to 1848; English kings to Kings of England, popes to Habemus Papam.

themes.name: Toy Box
themes.scope: Yes if it is a toy
themes.boundary: Toy Box: playthings; board and card games go to The Games Board, video games to Insert Coin, skateboards to Board Riders.
example_beats: LEGO brick as we know it (1958)

themes.name: African Kingdoms
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining moment of a sub-Saharan African kingdom or empire
themes.boundary: African Kingdoms: states ruled from Africa, Mansa Musa and Adwa included; outsiders' exploration and conquest go to Scramble for Africa, Kush's pharaohs to Pharaohs, Queen Nzinga to Crowned Queens.
example_beats: Ezana of Aksum converts to Christianity (330)
Askia the Great takes power in Songhai (1493)
Afonso I rules the Kingdom of Kongo (1506)

themes.name: Building Blocks
themes.scope: Yes if it is a discovery about atoms or the chemical elements
themes.boundary: Building Blocks owns the stuff matter is made of; bombs, reactors and arms control go to The Atomic Age, new materials to Material World, ideas about the cosmos to Cosmic Ideas.

themes.name: Let's Celebrate
themes.scope: Yes if it is a holiday, festival or parade
themes.boundary: Let's Celebrate: days and festivals people keep; music festivals and concerts go to Crowd Roars, calendars and daylight saving to Clockwork, May Day's labour origins to Down Tools.

themes.name: Stargazers
themes.scope: Yes if it is a telescope, or something new spotted through one
themes.boundary: Stargazers: telescopes and the planets, moons and stars they found, space telescopes included; ideas about what the universe is, such as the Big Bang, go to Cosmic Ideas, sky spectacles to Sky Show, spacecraft visits to Other Worlds.
example_beats: First exoplanet around a Sun-like star (1995)

themes.name: Temple Kingdoms
themes.scope: Yes if it is a king or kingdom of mainland Southeast Asia
themes.boundary: Temple Kingdoms: Khmer, Burmese, Thai and Vietnamese kingdoms; the Indonesian islands go to Indonesia, independence to Flags Come Down, city foundings to Capitals Founded.
example_beats: Jayavarman II proclaimed god-king at Angkor (802)
Vietnam defeats China at Bach Dang (938)
Gia Long founds the Nguyen dynasty (1802)

themes.name: Tune In
themes.scope: Yes if it is a radio or TV station or network
themes.boundary: Tune In: the stations and networks themselves; individual TV shows go to Prime Time, telegraph and telephone to Message Sent.
example_beats: BBC starts the first regular TV service (1936)
Voice of America goes on air (1942)

themes.name: Shogun!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining act of a samurai or shogun
themes.boundary: Shogun!: samurai rule up to the shogunate's end, the Mongol fleets of 1274 and 1281 included; Perry's Black Ships and the Meiji era go to Meiji Leap, anime and manga to Cool Japan.

themes.name: The Ballot Box
themes.scope: Yes if it is a landmark election or a new way of voting
themes.boundary: The Ballot Box owns elections and voting methods; women winning the vote go to Votes for Women, South Africa's 1994 vote shares with Civil Rights Road, constitutions to Law of the Land.

themes.name: Order Up!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous restaurant or food chain
themes.boundary: Order Up!: restaurants and chains; dishes go to Born in a Kitchen, coffee houses and bars to What We Drink, shops to Retail Therapy.
example_beats: White Castle opens, the first burger chain (1921)

themes.name: Law of the Land
themes.scope: Yes if it is a law code, charter or constitution
themes.boundary: Law of the Land: written law; trials and court rulings go to Day in Court, police and prisons to Crime & Punishment, Magna Carta shares with Kings of England.

themes.name: Native Nations
themes.scope: Yes if it is a battle, treaty or leader of a Native American nation
themes.boundary: Native Nations: Indigenous peoples of the US and Canada; Mesoamerica and the Andes go to Before Columbus, the Spanish conquest to Conquistadors, the Pueblo Revolt stays here.

themes.name: Stone Age Firsts
themes.scope: Yes if it is a find, site or achievement of Stone Age people
themes.boundary: Stone Age Firsts owns what early Homo sapiens made, dated to its making; hominin bones go to Bone Hunters, life before Homo sapiens to Before Us.
example_beats: Homo sapiens at Jebel Irhoud (300,000 BC)
Oldest cave art in Sulawesi (45,500 BC)

themes.name: The Raj
themes.scope: Yes if it is British rule in India, or the fight against it
themes.boundary: The Raj: Company and Crown rule and the freedom movement; the Mughal court goes to Peacock Throne, famines to Famine Years, and India's 1947 independence stays here.

themes.name: Back from the Brink
themes.scope: Yes if it is a step in protecting wildlife or wild places
themes.boundary: Back from the Brink owns conservation law, parks and rescues; extinctions go to Gone Forever, wild animals tamed for service to Tamed.

themes.name: Kings of Kings
themes.scope: Yes if it is a defining act of a Persian or Iranian king or dynasty
themes.boundary: Kings of Kings: Persia's rulers and dynasties; Persepolis burning goes to Cities Ablaze, Thermopylae to Against the Odds, Nader Shah's sack of Delhi to Peacock Throne.
example_beats: Cyrus founds the Achaemenid Empire (550 BC)
Darius carves the Behistun inscription (520 BC)

themes.name: Boom & Bust
themes.scope: Yes if it is a financial bubble, crash or bank failure
themes.boundary: Boom & Bust: markets breaking; frauds stay with Stolen!, currencies and hyperinflation with Hard Currency.

themes.name: Down Tools
themes.scope: Yes if it is a strike, a union or a workers' rights moment
themes.boundary: Down Tools owns labour history; peaceful mass protests go to Take to the Streets, communist movements to Red Flags.

themes.name: Royal Weddings
themes.scope: Yes if it is a royal wedding
themes.boundary: Royal Weddings owns royal marriages; queens who ruled go to Crowned Queens, the founding of states to Nations of Europe.
example_beats: Wang Zhaojun marries the Xiongnu khan (33 BC)

themes.name: Insert Coin
themes.scope: Yes if it is a video game or game console
themes.boundary: Insert Coin: video games and consoles, Japanese ones included; table games and machines that beat us at them go to The Games Board, non-game gadgets to In Your Pocket.

themes.name: Wild Weather
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous storm, flood, heatwave or other extreme weather
themes.boundary: Wild Weather owns extreme weather; quakes and eruptions go to When the Earth Moved, fires to Cities Ablaze, droughts that starved people to Famine Years.

themes.name: Palaces & Power
themes.scope: Yes if it is the building of a palace or seat of government
themes.boundary: Palaces & Power: where rulers lived and governed; castles and forts built for defence go to Walls & Fortresses, the Forbidden City stays with Mandate of Heaven, Versailles with Kings of France.

themes.name: All Aboard!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a railway line, locomotive or famous train
themes.boundary: All Aboard! owns the railway between towns; city metros, trams and buses go to Mind the Gap, bridges and tunnels to Bridges & Tunnels.

themes.name: Look It Up
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous dictionary, encyclopedia or other reference book
themes.boundary: Look It Up: reference works in print; newspapers go to Front Pages, typefaces to Letters & Type, Wikipedia to Going Online.
example_beats: First part of the Oxford English Dictionary (1884)

themes.name: Sky Show
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous comet, eclipse, supernova, meteor or aurora
themes.boundary: Sky Show: spectacles seen from Earth; telescopes and new worlds go to Stargazers, the ideas they inspired, Eddington's eclipse included, to Cosmic Ideas.
example_beats: Earth passes through Halley's comet's tail (1910)

themes.name: Step Right Up
themes.scope: Yes if it is a world's fair, amusement park or fairground ride
themes.boundary: Step Right Up: crowds out for the spectacle; record-height towers go to Tallest in the World, lasting modern buildings to Modern Marvels, circuses and stage shows to On Stage.
example_beats: Great Exhibition at the Crystal Palace (1851)

themes.name: Plant Hunters
themes.scope: Yes if it is a crop or plant that spread across the world
themes.boundary: Plant Hunters owns plants on the move; farm tools and methods go to Plow & Harvest, drinks to What We Drink, starvation to Famine Years.
example_beats: Wickham smuggles rubber seeds out of Brazil (1876)

themes.name: Household Gadgets
themes.scope: Yes if it is an appliance or gadget for the home
themes.boundary: Household Gadgets: machines for the home; lighting goes to Let There Be Light, food preserving to Food Tech, portable gadgets to In Your Pocket.
example_beats: Mechanical dishwasher patented by Josephine Cochrane (1886)

themes.name: Reading the Rocks
themes.scope: Yes if it is a landmark of geology
themes.boundary: Reading the Rocks owns discoveries about the Earth itself; quakes and eruptions go to When the Earth Moved, fossils to Bone Hunters, scales such as Richter's to Taking Measure.
example_beats: Mohorovicic finds the base of the crust (1909)

themes.name: Silk Road
themes.scope: Yes if it is an event on the Silk Road
themes.boundary: Silk Road: the overland caravans and what travelled with them; steppe conquests go to Horse Lords, embassies between courts to Face to Face, the Black Death to Plague Years, the Diamond Sutra to Letters & Type, Constantinople's fall to Sublime Porte.
example_beats: Zhang Qian sets out for the West (138 BC)
The Travels of Marco Polo published (1300)

themes.name: Safety in Numbers
themes.scope: Yes if it is the founding of an alliance or international organisation
themes.boundary: Safety in Numbers: alliances and international bodies; war-ending treaties go to Peace at Last, borders to Lines on a Map, sports bodies to their own sport's theme, OPEC to Black Gold.
example_beats: Treaty of Rome creates the EEC (1957)

themes.name: Prime Time
themes.scope: Yes if it is a TV show
themes.boundary: Prime Time: the shows, animated sitcoms included; channels and networks go to Tune In, cartoon films to Drawn to Life, Korean dramas share with Korean Wave.
themes.notes: Spread the shows across every decade, from the first TV shows to now.

themes.name: Born in a Kitchen
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous dish or snack
themes.boundary: Born in a Kitchen: dishes and snacks cooks invented; desserts and sweets go to Sweet Tooth, factory foods to Food Tech, restaurants to Order Up!
example_beats: The sandwich named for Lord Sandwich (1762)
The hamburger arrives at Louis' Lunch (1900)
The Cronut debuts in New York (2013)

themes.name: Flags Come Down
themes.scope: Yes if it is a colony gaining independence, or a decisive step toward it
themes.boundary: Flags Come Down: decolonisation worldwide; India goes to The Raj, Indonesia to Indonesia, Latin America's wars of independence to The Liberators.
example_beats: Hong Kong handed back to China (1997)

themes.name: Fright Night
themes.scope: Yes if it is a horror story or film
themes.boundary: Fright Night: works made to frighten, Frankenstein included; science fiction and fantasy go to Beyond the Stars, detective fiction to Whodunit, Godzilla to Cool Japan.

themes.name: Retail Therapy
themes.scope: Yes if it is a great market or a new way to shop
themes.boundary: Retail Therapy: markets and ways of shopping; the founding of shop chains goes to Still Trading, advertising to Sell, Sell, Sell, money and credit cards to Hard Currency, restaurants to Order Up!
example_beats: Bon Marche, the first department store (1852)

themes.name: Coup!
themes.scope: Yes if it is a coup, putsch or military takeover
themes.boundary: Coup! owns seizures of power by plot or force from above; popular uprisings go to Rise Up!, forced abdications to Abdicated!.

themes.name: Strike a Chord
themes.scope: Yes if it is a musical instrument, or a famous model of one
themes.boundary: Strike a Chord: the instruments themselves; recording and selling go to Press Play, styles of music and dance to Born to Groove.

themes.name: Bone Hunters
themes.scope: Yes if it is a famous fossil discovery
themes.boundary: Bone Hunters owns fossil finds, dinosaurs and early humans included; prehistoric events themselves go to Before Us, ancient human sites to Stone Age Firsts.
example_beats: Neanderthal found in the Neander valley (1856)
